export-explorer-publish-replaces-both.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: publish() caught every exception, KeyboardInterrupt included, and restored the previous public/data and public/evidence before re-raising. The Rust command cannot catch a signal, because the crate forbids unsafe code, so the Python front ignores SIGINT while export-explorer publish runs: an interrupt in that window no longer stops publication. Both moves finish, or a failed move restores the previous pair as before, so public/ always holds a complete pair. Compatibility impact: Ctrl-C during the two moves publishes the new export where Python kept the old one; SIGTERM ends both as before. tools/test_export_explorer.py checks that SIGINT is ignored only while publish runs, and the cargo tests a_failed_move_restores_the_previous_pair, a_failed_restoration_keeps_the_backups and a_failed_first_publication_leaves_no_directories pin the restoration.

export-explorer-iso-24-midnight.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py read review timing with the running interpreter's datetime.fromisoformat. The Rust parser follows Python 3.14's, for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter: an hour of 24 with zero minutes, seconds and microseconds is the next midnight, and a decimal mark after the hour or minute, a decimal mark with no digits before the zone and a fourth colon-separated field are refused. Compatibility impact: a review whose dispatch or end time uses one of those forms changes between a duration and null. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses: 3.12 refused an hour of 24 and parsed the malformed forms, such as 10.5, 10:00.5, 10:00:00.Z, 10:00:00:00 and the offset +01:00.5; a generated differential of 297,892 strings found 980 that 3.12 refuses and 3.14 parses, all hour 24, and 2,020 that 3.12 parses and 3.14 refuses, with no other difference. Python 3.13 differs in the same way on 980 and 1,495 of them. Older interpreters differ more: Python 3.10 parses only the forms datetime.isoformat writes, refusing 6,688 of those strings that 3.14 parses. The Rust parser matched Python 3.14 on all 694,284 strings of two such differentials, and all 2,807 tracked attempt times parse alike under 3.12 and 3.14. This case pins 60.0 seconds from 23:59:00 to 24:00:00.

export-explorer-mixed-token-sum.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py summed output tokens with the running interpreter's sum(). The Rust sum follows Python 3.14's: exact 64-bit integers, then from the first float a compensated (Neumaier) sum that adds each later integer as a correctly rounded float with compensation, then ordinary addition past 64 bits. Compatibility impact: only a requests file that mixes float and integer counts, where an integer follows a float, can change in its last bits. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses, and Python 3.13, an integer after a float was added without compensation, so [1e16, 1, 1] summed to 1e16 where 3.14 gives 1.0000000000000002e16. Python 3.11 and older did not compensate float sums at all, so ten 0.1 counts summed to 0.9999999999999999 where 3.12 and later give 1.0. No tracked requests file holds a float count.

export-explorer-unsortable-manifestation.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. From local independent review of #198: the v1 case gave its integer claim ids a null family_id, so the export skipped them before sorting and the case pinned exit 0 with no manifestations; it now links both claims to GT-t1 and pins the refusal. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py sorted family manifestations and configuration models with sorted(), which orders any mutually comparable values, such as integers. The Rust export sorts text, as every schema-valid claim id and recorded model is, and refuses two or more values that are not all text with TypeError, exit 1, rather than reproduce Python's ordering of numbers and booleans. A list with one value is kept as it is, as Python keeps it. Compatibility impact: none for schema-valid current facts, under any interpreter; facts edited to hold such values exported in Python and are now refused. On these facts the base export wrote manifestations [1, 2]; the Rust export exits 1 after staging the evidence it reached first.

export-explorer-lone-surrogate-facts.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py kept a lone surrogate escape from a current document as Python text, exported it when no published field held it, and failed with UnicodeEncodeError, exit 1, when one did. The Rust facts reader refuses every lone surrogate escape with ValueError, exit 1, as bench-tools' JSON reader does. In the same way the Python front writes the facts with json.dumps(allow_nan=False), as #198 specifies, so a NaN or infinite number anywhere in the current documents is refused with ValueError, exit 1; Python exported one outside the published fields and refused a NaN inside them as 'staged dataset differs from the export'. tools/test_export_explorer.py pins the non-finite refusal. Compatibility impact: none for the repository; its current facts hold neither, which the full export checks on every build.

export-explorer-evidence-reads-every-inp.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. By the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19; resolved by #198. Changes behavior on purpose: export_explorer.py restored each missing evidence file as the export reached it, so a missing, unrestorable packet failed with 'missing or changed evidence' before a later input was read. export-explorer evidence reads every input before the Python front restores anything, so the unreadable normalized.json fails first, with json's message. A retained-backups refusal likewise comes after restoration. Compatibility impact: when an export has both an input error and missing evidence, the input error is reported and no evidence is restored; an export with either one alone fails as before.

export-explorer-unicode-15-1-adjudicatio.reason: Adopt for #198, porting the export of tools/export_explorer.py to the Rust export-explorer, part of #154, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration on 2026-10-19. Diagnostics keep the Python program name export_explorer.py. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. export_explorer.py's KeyError and other diagnostics quoted input with repr, which followed the running interpreter's Unicode database, so it escaped characters that database lacked. The Rust export quotes with the bench-tools repr, which escapes exactly the code points Python 3.14's str.isprintable() rejects (Unicode 16.0), for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: a quoted value changes when it holds a character assigned after the former interpreter's Unicode version. Against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), that is 5,812 code points, those added in Unicode 15.1 and 16.0, which 3.12 escapes and Rust writes as-is; none the other way. Older interpreters differ on more: Python 3.13 (Unicode 15.1) on 5,185, the Unicode 16.0 additions, and Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) on 11,130. This case pins U+2EBF0, added in Unicode 15.1, in a claim's adjudication id that no decision has: the base export on Python 3.12 printed KeyError: 'probe-\U0002ebf0'; Rust writes the character, as the base export did on Python 3.13 and 3.14.
